bottom_line: In the open-label STELLAR trial, over 6 weeks rosuvastatin 10 to 40 mg reduced non-HDL-C by 42.0% to 50.9% compared with 34.4% to 48.1% with atorvastatin, 26.0% to 41.8% with simvastatin, and 18.6% to 27.4% with pravastatin.
implications: Over 6 weeks in this open-label trial, the reported least squares mean percentage reductions in non-HDL-C and apo B were larger with rosuvastatin 10–40 mg than with the stated dose comparisons (e.g., non-HDL-C 42.0% to 50.9% vs 34.4% to 48.1% with atorvastatin). These data support conclusions about short-term changes in lipids/apolipoproteins and ratios as reported, but do not establish effects on clinical outcomes in this document ("The studies investigating the impact of rosuvastatin therapy on clinical out-comes are ongoing.").

major_points.text: Randomized, multicenter, parallel-group, open-label trial with 6-week treatment period.
major_points.quote: In this randomized, multicenter, parallel-group, open-label trial (4522IL/0065)

major_points.text: Patients were adults with hypercholesterolemia defined by LDL-C and triglyceride thresholds.
major_points.quote: patients with hypercholesterolemia (LDL-C >160 mg/dL and <250 mg/dL and triglycerides <400 mg/dL)

major_points.text: Interventions were multiple dose ranges of rosuvastatin, atorvastatin, simvastatin, and pravastatin given once daily for 6 weeks.
major_points.quote: patients >18 years of age received rosuvastatin 10, 20, 40, or 80 mg; atorvastatin 10, 20, 40, or 80 mg; simvastatin 10, 20, 40, or 80 mg; or pravastatin 10, 20, or 40 mg for 6 weeks.

major_points.text: Pairwise comparisons were prospectively planned between rosuvastatin 10, 20, and 40 mg and milligram-equivalent or higher doses of comparators.
major_points.quote: Pairwise comparisons were prospectively planned and performed between rosuvastatin 10, 20, and 40 mg and milligram-equivalent or higher doses of comparators.

major_points.text: Non-HDL-C was calculated as total cholesterol minus HDL-C.
major_points.quote: Non-HDL-C was calculated by subtracting HDL-C from TC.

major_points.text: Analysis used analysis of variance with Bonferroni adjustment; P values <0.002 considered significant.
major_points.quote: P values were <0.002 (using the Bonferroni adjustment for multiple comparisons)
